title: The Generator Ban That Sent Sunil Mittal to a Taiwan Phone Fair
conflicts: Ban and Taiwan dates: Mittal (HBS 2017) puts the Taiwan fair in October 1982 after the ban; Vir Sanghvi dates the ban to 1983; story says 'early 1980s' for the ban and attributes October 1982 to Mittal. Where he first saw the phone: Taiwan trade fair (Mittal, Sanghvi) versus a Singapore hawker (MBA Review 2009); story follows Mittal. Starting capital $1,500 (Wharton, MBA Review) versus Rs 20,000 (Dataquest); story uses $1,500.
notes: Episode set at the early-1980s turn from generator imports to telephones (the real move into telecoms) rather than the 1995 Airtel launch, which is mentioned only as the outcome. Includes Sanghvi's report that Mittal admitted the early component imports may well have been illegal, attributed to Sanghvi. Main source is the HBS Creating Emerging Markets oral-history transcript (PDF behind an expiring signed link; the stable HBS page is cited).
